areas.summary:
Classes are in good shape for making objects and constructing them. Across 135 programs on build 0124:
- Objects work with no constructor, a zero-argument one, or one taking any of the nine built types, a list, a map or another object.
- Field initialisers work for every type, and each object gets its own list and map fields.
- Spacesuit-typed and self-typed fields work: linked lists, trees, 3000-deep recursion through objects.
- Each loop iteration makes a fresh object, and factories returning objects work.
- Reference semantics hold for =, parameters and list items; containers are copied because they are values.
- Constructor order is supertype first, arguments reach the nearest constructor, and dispatch during construction runs the subtype's capsule.
- Wrong argument COUNT is refused before running, even through included files and nested spacesuits. Redeclaring a name makes a new object, and satellite.class works everywhere satellite.spacesuit does.
- Objects are freed when unreferenced, and making one costs about a capsule call.

Problems found:
- A-06 (high): a constructor that declares an object of its own spacesuit is not refused and grew to 5 GB in 3 s and 24 GB in 22 s. The field form of the same ring IS refused, and that refusal's advice ('give it an object in satellite.constructor') leads to it.
- A-01, A-02 (refused-late, medium): type mismatches are never checked before running. This covers a wrong-type argument even as a literal (any capsule, not just constructors), an object of the wrong spacesuit into a typed name, parameter or list, and a literal into an object name. In an untaken branch these exit 0.
- A-05 (memory, medium): objects in a reference cycle (self-link, parent/child back-link) are never freed. Breaking the link by hand frees them. The help doesn't say this; internally it is tied to the owed .pointer().
- Missing, with no word at all: object comparison or identity (A-04, and == is refused only at run time), a test for an empty object field (A-03, so lists need a bool flag), this/self for an object to hand itself on (A-13), static members (A-12, and no globals), a second constructor (A-09, refused cleanly), copy/clone (A-10) and a destructor (A-11). Working workarounds are noted for each.
- Low: a constructor inside satellite.protected is silently public (A-08). An object declared in an untaken branch is refused as 'no capsule named get' (A-07).

Known issues hit again and not re-reported: 037 (spacesuit names like xa), 042 (a capsule called on an empty field), 043/071 ('text' + obj), 072 (cell.make_one()), 028 (object map keys).

areas.summary:
I ran about 150 programs on satl build 0124 covering capsules on objects, sections, answers and access. The core of this area is solid. All of these work correctly: public and protected sections; bare calls between a spacesuit's own capsules in any order; parameters of six types; answers of every type, including objects of the spacesuit's own type; containers answered as copies; long chains; method calls in every expression position with left-to-right order; tail and mutual recursion; objects of one spacesuit working on each other, including protected capsules on a sibling; dynamic dispatch through three levels and base-typed lists and parameters; over 100 built-in method words used as capsule names; and top-level, namespace and included-file capsules resolved from inside methods. The name-clash, access, argument-count and override rules are all enforced before anything runs, with clear sentences.

Middle self-calls no longer crash: 1,000,000 deep works on methods, following the author's 2026-09-25 reversal.

Four medium problems:
- **B-01:** an override that never answers is refused only at run time when the supertype's capsule uses it; the direct call is caught before anything runs.
- **B-02:** a spacesuit's capsule called on a method's answer that is not an object gets a false "math sign spacing" or "undecided operator" reason.
- **B-03:** two objects cannot be compared with `==` (refused, and only at run time), although `list.contains` already compares objects by identity.
- **B-04:** `satellite.return(f(...))` is never treated as a tail call, so any recursion that answers a value costs about 9 KB a level (100,000 deep = 904 MB). The call-then-`satellite.return()` form stays at 21 MB for 1,000,000.

Missing class features, with no word for them in words.tsv (the author decides whether the language wants them):
- calling the supertype's version of a replaced capsule (B-05)
- a name for the object itself inside its own capsules, so it can be answered or handed on (B-06)
- a type test before a downcast (B-07)
- destructor (B-08)
- class-level (static) members (B-09)
- abstract capsules (B-10)
- copying or cloning an object (no word found)

Two low findings: B-11, where an undeclared alias spelling (`o.contains()`) silently runs a declared `has()` (same cause as 004, different effect), and B-12, where a capsule written outside every section is said to be "inside the satellite.protected part".

Known items I hit again: 045 (`[ ]` after an answer), 072 (a capsule called on the spacesuit's own name), 081 (S240 points at the header line), 049 ("so far no type has it"), and 004 (`o.string()` runs `to_string()`).

Outside my area, not reported: `&&` is refused in conditions; an empty map written `= {}` is refused at run time (the help says to write nothing after the name); fraction `+` is not built.

All programs and outputs are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-madness-code-cxx-satellite/ae1d0a71-fb22-4236-98c5-a21ef75df170/scratchpad/probe/B-methods (bNN.satl / bNN.out).

areas.summary:
Inheritance and polymorphism in satl build 0124 are in good shape for everything the help documents. I ran 117 programs. Four-deep chains work: fields and capsules of every level are reachable, every constructor runs supertype-first and arguments reach the nearest one. Dispatch follows the object's own spacesuit through every holder: a supertype-typed name, parameter, list, map, field, a thread argument, and tail calls. Template methods with protected hooks work, as do shadowed fields as two slots, and extending spacesuits of other files, further down the file, or nested. Override rules (same access or wider, same parameters) are enforced before running with clear sentences. Decorator, composite (50,000 deep) and factory patterns run, and dispatch through 10 levels costs about the same as a direct call.

Problems. One high: C-01, a supertype constructor that makes an object of its own subtype neither is refused nor crashes. It takes memory at about 1.9 GB a second, and I stopped each run after a few seconds so the machine would not run out. Plain endless recursion behaves the same way, so the cause is general, but the checker already refuses the same ring when it goes through a field. Two diagnostics are wrong or late: satellite.access on a supertype-typed name lists capsules the checker then refuses (C-02), and an override that never answers is caught only at run when called through a supertype name (C-03). areas.summary:
Nesting, files, namespaces and data structures built from spacesuits mostly work on build 0124. Nesting three deep, protected inner spacesuits, file.Type, file.outer.inner, five-part paths (file.namespace.outer.inner.inmost), subtypes across files and namespaces, use above the declaring line, lexical scoping of bare calls, and every name clash I tried behave correctly. Almost all refusals come before anything runs, with sentences that fit. A 1,000-node linked list, a doubly-linked list, a BST (recursive and iterative walks), an N-ary tree and a cyclic graph walked breadth-first all give right answers. Recursion through objects is fine to 50,000 deep.

The gaps for real data structures are about empty links and memory:
- **D-02:** there is no way to test whether a spacesuit field is empty.
- **D-03:** a field can never be emptied again. Linked structures need a bool marker or a 0-or-1 item list field, and both work.
- **D-04:** reference cycles are never freed (M26 plans a cycle collector later).
- **D-05:** a last call to the same capsule on another object, the natural recursive list walk, costs ~10 KB of memory a node.
- **D-01 (high):** a constructor that makes an object of its own spacesuit is not caught by the ring check, and at run it takes ~1.5 GB/s (21.7 GB in 15 s before my timeout). The ring refusal's own advice leads there.
- **D-06 (medium):** a wrong-spacesuit argument, assignment or append is refused only when its line runs; built types behave the same.

The rest is low-severity: no self/this, no object ==, no way to order a list of objects, a subtype can't name its supertype's nested spacesuit bare, and five refusal wordings.

All programs and outputs are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-madness-code-cxx-satellite/ae1d0a71-fb22-4236-98c5-a21ef75df170/scratchpad/probe/D-nesting. I ran q03 once only (it reached 21.7 GB); q04/q05/q06 ran under a 2-second cap. No thread programs were run.

areas.summary:
I ran about 130 programs against the installed satl (build 0124). Objects work with every container, with threads, with files, and on memory, apart from reference cycles.

**What works (all checked by output):**
- **Containers:** objects work in list<T>, map<string, T>, multiple<T, ...> and nested containers:
  - append, insert, remove, contains, index_of, first/last, truncate
  - list literals written with object names
  - for-loops calling a capsule on each item
  - calls on m[k] and grid[i][j]
- **Matching and copying:** list/map matching is by identity. A copied list, or a list passed to a capsule, is a new list whose objects are shared, with Java-like parameter rebinding.
- **Fields:** list and map fields are per object and handed out as copies. Composition and chained calls work.
- **Dispatch:** dynamic dispatch works through container items and supertype names, including to_string() overrides.
- **satellite.access:** it describes objects, lists, maps and multiples of objects, and fields inside capsules.
- **Threads** (never more than 2 per program):
  - thread.new(obj.capsule(args)) with join/wait answers, including object and list answers
  - overrides run on threads, and a protected capsule can be started by bare name
  - obj.lock() gave exact counts on every run (6000/12000), directly and through list items, map items and nested items
  - two threads appending new objects to a locked object's list field: 2000
- **Files:** an object with a file field writes, reads and closes through its capsules. Two objects sharing one locked file on two threads wrote 400 lines, 200 each.
- **Memory stays flat** for objects made and dropped in a loop (19.8 MB at 1k vs 19.9 MB at 100k), for objects local to a capsule, and for 100k objects in a list that is cleared.

**Class-level gaps:**
- **E-01:** a == b on two objects is refused, even for the same object, though list ==, contains and index_of already compare by identity.
- **E-02:** a list of objects cannot be ordered: by_value, max and min refuse, and there is no sort by key.
- **E-09:** there is no type test, and a wrong downcast stops the program.
- **E-10:** there is no copy or clone word.
- **E-07 (memory):** reference cycles are never freed. 50k two-object cycles take 45.8 MB vs 21.8 MB at 1k (185 MB when each object also holds an 8-number list). A self-cycle and an object in its own list field leak too. One-way links and cycles broken by hand are freed. This matches the documented 'cycle collector later'.

**Smaller issues:**
- **E-03:** by_name has the same to_string bug as 043.
- **E-04:** displaying a list of objects exits 14 but a map of objects exits 27, for the same sentence.
- **E-05:** access on a supertype-typed name lists subtype capsules that the checker refuses.
- **E-06:** a 079 variant: `all[n].call_put(n)`.
- **E-08:** a capsule called on a multiple holding a number is another way into 042.
- **E-11:** the bracketless memory words fail late with 'no value here'. args.memory.used is the machine's memory, so no word measures the program's own.
- **E-12:** speed note: a method call costs about 0.7 µs more than a capsule call, and each field initializer about 0.7 µs per object made. These were measured under load 13.8.
- **E-13:** an object given to a built-type name is refused only at run. This is language-wide.

**Known issues hit, not re-reported:**
- 021: thread.new(m["k"].call_add(5)) is refused with a false S721.
- 028: map<item, number> is accepted, then refused at the first write.
- 045: b.call_nums()[2] is refused.

All programs are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-madness-code-cxx-satellite/ae1d0a71-fb22-4236-98c5-a21ef75df170/scratchpad/probe/E-meets-language (the f*.satl files are the minimal versions).

verified.overall:
All 58 findings were re-run on build 0124 from /tmp/claude-1000/-home-madness-code-cxx-satellite/ae1d0a71-fb22-4236-98c5-a21ef75df170/scratchpad/probe/verify. All reproduce except E-12's timing claim. After merging: 24 confirmed, 5 by-design, 6 already-known, 1 not-reproduced and 22 duplicates. The three constructor-ring programs were stopped at 2 s instead of 20 because they grow about 1.5 GB/s.

SOLID: the basics of classes work. A copy of tests/spacesuits.satl (with spacesuit_parts.satl) runs to exit 0 on 0124. That covers: declaring spacesuits and objects; fields; constructors with arguments; protected and public, enforced before anything runs (S230); objects as references; objects in lists, as parameters and as answers; spacesuits from included files; nested spacesuits (outer.inner); single inheritance; dynamic dispatch; overrides checked for access and parameters; subtypes reaching protected members bare; and a downcast checked at run. Most refusals come before anything runs and are accurate.

BROKEN, in order of impact:
(1) A-06 (with C-01 and D-01 as duplicates): a constructor that makes an object of its own spacesuit, or of a subtype, is not refused. It uses memory at about 1.5 GB/s, although the field form of the same ring is refused, and that refusal's advice leads straight to this program. The only high finding.
(2) Type mismatches are judged only at run, after earlier lines have printed. A-02 covers an object of the wrong spacesuit, or a literal, given to an object name, parameter or list (duplicates C-04, D-06, E-13). A-01 is a literal given to a parameter: the half of ERRORS2 #8 that ERRORS3 marks FIXED but 0da03d9 never covered. B-01 (with C-03) is an override that never answers, which is also caught only at run.
(3) Tail calls: satellite.return(self(...)) is never collapsed (B-04, about 9 KB a level), and the same capsule called last on another object is not collapsed either (D-05). So a recursive capsule that answers a value, or a recursive walk down a linked list, grows with depth. The author decides whether his 'last line' ruling covers these forms.
(4) Low-severity wording: C-02 (satellite.access lists a subtype's capsules on a supertype name), B-12 (a loose capsule said to be 'inside the satellite.protected part'), C-12, A-07, D-09, D-10, D-11, D-12, D-14.
Already known and still present: 004 (B-11), 042 (B-02, E-08), 043 (E-03, E-04), 079 (E-06).

MISSING (the author decides), ordered by how much each stops a normal program:
- No null: an empty object field cannot be tested or cleared (A-03). This is what makes linked lists and trees awkward.
- Objects cannot be compared with ==, even for identity, although list == and .contains already compare by identity (E-01).
- No way for an object to refer to itself: no this or self, so no back-links, registration or chaining (A-13).
- No call to the supertype's version of an overridden capsule (B-05).
- No type test before a downcast (E-09).
- No sorting of objects by a key or a capsule's answer (E-02).
- Smaller gaps: no static members (A-12), no abstract capsules (C-07), no copy (A-10), no destructor (A-11), and nested spacesuits are not inherited by bare name (C-09).

BY DESIGN: the reference-cycle leak (A-05, with D-04 and E-07) is the author's conceded M26 decision: refcount now, .pointer() as a weak reference, a cycle collector later. The 004 help does not mention it, and without a null value a cycle can only be broken by re-pointing a field at a sentinel object. Also by design: A-08 and A-09 (one constructor, public wherever written: suit_scan.cpp:251) and C-08 (the supertype-arguments rule; M35's satellite.supertype is the planned answer).
